text:
Predicates:
Cost(x, y) ::: it costs x to take the y test.
FinancialAid(x, y) ::: x provides financial aid to y.
EconomicHardship(x) ::: x proves economic hardship.
Applicant(x, y) ::: x is a y applicant.
Difficulty(x, y) ::: x has difficulty caused by y.
Parent(x, y) ::: x is a y-parent family.
Unemployed(x, y) ::: x has been out of work for y.
Premises:
Cost(205, gre) ::: It costs US $205 to take the GRE test.
∀x (Applicant(x, gre) ∧ EconomicHardship(x) → FinancialAid(ets, x)) ::: ETS provides financial aid to those GRE applicants who prove economic hardship.
∀x (EconomicHardship(x) → ∃y (Difficulty(x, y) ∧ (y = littleMoney ∨ y = fewResources))) ::: Economic hardship refers to difficulty caused by having too little money or too few resources.
Parent(tom, single) ::: Tom lives in a single-parent family.
Unemployed(dad, moreThanYear) ::: His dad has been out of work for more than a year.
Conclusion:
Applicant(tom, gre) ∧ EconomicHardship(tom) ::: Tom can apply for financial aid from ETS to take the GRE test.
